newsitem.title: USA: US Midcontinent diesel basis eases on stock build.
newsitem.headline: US Midcontinent diesel basis eases on stock build.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials eased Wednesday on estimates of a build in regional distillate stocks over the past week, traders said.

Distillate inventories increased more than one million barrels last week in the Midwest PADD 2 market and were 3.8 million barrels above last year's levels, the American Petroleum Institute said late Tuesday.
Gasoline differentials were steady in the spot Chicago and Group Three markets on a 631,000 barrel draw in gasoline inventories in the PADD 2 region reported in the API's weekly stocks estimates.

Traders were skeptical of the weekly estimates provided to the Washington, D.C.-based trade group by the nation's refiners, noting sharp revisions in the crude and gasoline estimates from prior weeks.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was bid 2.75 cents a gallon over May NYMEX unleaded for all April timings, with high sulphur talked 4.75/5.0 cents over the print.
Group Three high and low sulphur was bid 6.25 cents a gallon over the print for prompt and later deliveries.
Chicago unleaded was talked 0.50/0,75 cent a gallon over May NYMEX unleaded, with premium easing to 5.50 cents higher.
Group Three unleaded for prompt and later April deliveries was talked 0.50/0.25 cent a gallon under the print, with premium 3.50 cents higher.
